Problem & context Objectives My role & project work Technical implementation Engineering decisions Challenges & solutions Testing & verification Current status Lessons & next steps

Architecture

Application tier → Security group → Private subnets → RDS MySQL

Problem & context

A database should be reachable by its application tier without broad public network access.

Objectives

Practice RDS MySQL subnet placement, application-to-database connectivity and access rules.

My role & project work

Documented an RDS MySQL lab covering private DB subnet groups, application-security-group ingress and connection checks.

Technical implementation

The README records creation of a DB subnet group, MySQL ingress restricted to an application security group, disabled public access and database connection verification. It also discusses Multi-AZ and managed credential storage.

Engineering decisions

Express database access in terms of the application tier rather than open internet ingress. Keep conceptual discussion separate from demonstrated deployment results.

Challenges & solutions

Database connectivity depends on subnet placement and security-group rules. Current failover and restoration results require execution logs that are not supplied in the repository.

Testing & verification

Reviewed README and the architecture asset inventory at revision f8566401b686ab69cf27b67c299c60e13fa0c2dc. No IaC, automated database tests or measured failure logs are present. The README's service descriptions and cost/performance statements were not adopted as verified claims.

Current status

Documentation-backed lab. No measured recovery time, data-loss guarantee or current AWS deployment status is claimed.

Lessons & next steps

Subnet groups, connectivity tests and least-privilege ingress form useful practical evidence. A reproducible restore exercise would strengthen the project.
